title: De la conjecture au noyau Lean : réseaux optimaux, énergies quantiques et génétique des populations — démonstrations humaines, Lean 4, rusty-SUNDIALS et LeanFlow (manuel pour les classes préparatoires et les écoles d'ingénieurs)
description:
A 175-page French textbook for CPGE students (MPSI, MP2I, MP, MPI) and engineering schools. An English university edition is published alongside it. It tells the story of a year of formalisation as it really happened: conjectures, human proofs, Lean 4 statements checked by the kernel, numerical solutions, and refutations. Every result is shown three times: as a step-by-step human proof, as a Lean 4 statement, and as a computation with rusty-SUNDIALS (CVODE in Rust) and LeanFlow (data certificates checked by Lean), on public Hugging Face datasets.

Chapters: (1) foundations: lattices, Poisson summation, completely monotone functions, and formal verification; (2) the flow of formalisations, from universal optimality to physical potentials and the Sandier–Serfaty conjecture; (3) a quantum surprise: zero-point energy can make the triangular lattice lose its optimality; (4) population genetics in Lean, from Moran fixation to the isothermal theorem; (5) five use cases (dipolar excitons, Yukawa crystals, superfluid helium, a shell model, fixation of a mutation) with data, code and certificates. Appendices: A, analysis; B, finite Markov chains and martingales; C, Lean 4 for beginners (compiled examples, including a forgery that the kernel replay rejects); D, certified numerics; E, a step-by-step reproduction guide; F, 12 worked Python, Rust and LeanFlow examples, each with real output.

Confidence levels (Elenchus). Every claim carries a level. A: kernel-checked Lean, meaning the axioms lie within {propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound}, a leanchecker kernel replay passed, and a search found no construct that bypasses the kernel. Modules without a recorded replay are marked 'A sans rejeu' (A without replay). L: literature. C: a human argument. X: floating point, which never supports a claim.

Honesty. The results were produced by AI agents (Claude) under the author's direction and audited by separate AI agents: chapters 1–5 ACCEPT_WITH_CORRECTIONS, appendices ACCEPT_WITH_CORRECTIONS, both revised. No human mathematician has reviewed them. Several results depend on openai/math theorems, which are AI-generated and not peer reviewed. The Sandier–Serfaty conjecture is NOT proved here. The Navier–Stokes chapter reports an independent rebuild and kernel replay of a third-party corpus and makes no claim that a Clay problem is solved. Negative results (a refuted conjecture, a method that does not extend, a transition that does not occur) are reported as such.

Dedicated to Ilene, Alexis and Aurelia. Five acronym theorems, rfl-checked re-exports of kernel-checked results, are hidden in the Lean code for the attentive reader.
notes: Textbook (French, CPGE level), v1. Each chapter and the appendices were written independently from one fact sheet (FACTS.md) and then audited independently (AUDIT.md, AUDIT_APPENDICES.md, with REVISION files). The full list of DOIs cited is in the bibliography. The code is in AutoevolveAI papers/textbook_formalisation_2026/code; the Rust examples are rusty-SUNDIALS crate qf-textbook-examples (PR #81, commit f01b82b).
